summary: Router 0.22.2 hardens the control UI (ADR-0065). Defect: ui.html put values into inline event handlers as onclick="f('${esc(x)}')"; esc() did not escape the single quote, and HTML entities are decoded before handler JavaScript runs, so a model name reported by a node (controlled by a compromised approved agent) could break out of the string and run script in the operator's browser, where same-origin script can call admin APIs. Fix: esc() also escapes the single quote; new js(s) = esc(JSON.stringify(String(s))); all 53 quoted interpolations in inline handlers (model, role, client, setting, node fingerprint and version values, the node name inside a confirm text, the copy-token label) now use ${js(...)}; only a numeric loop index and the fixed property names canary/shadow remain unquoted. New browser_headers.install adds via on_response_prepare (setdefault, a handler's own header wins): on the control port Content-Security-Policy default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self' and X-Frame-Options DENY; on both ports X-Content-Type-Options nosniff and Referrer-Policy no-referrer; no CORS header anywhere. test/dev_env.py now sets control_auth.allow_unauthenticated_loopback (it removed control_auth, which answers 503 since ADR-0053).

findings.evidence: A model name with a single quote rendered into onclick="measure('...')" broke out of the JavaScript string; the control port sent no CSP or framing protection.
findings.resolution: Handler values as JSON string literals, CSP with connect-src 'self' and frame-ancestors 'none', companion headers; checked in CI and once in a browser. 'unsafe-inline' remains.
